title: A Colony for the Protocol
premise: Xanthe Reyes investigates 'impossible accidents' for the Meridian Compact, the insurance syndicate that quietly governs the colonies after the interstellar network went silent. A salvage ship, the Vesper Kite, returns from the dead relay at Tau Ceti with its crew aged backward—memories intact but bodies decades younger—carrying proof that the Compact itself caused the Silence to hide a failed terraforming atrocity. As Xanthe digs, she discovers her own missing years are a redacted entry in the same ledger, and that the Compact plans to wake only its loyal half of the cryosleep fleet while letting the rest drift forever. In the end she broadcasts the full ledger to every sleeper ship at once, forcing the Compact to wake everyone or be overthrown by the waking, and chooses to stand trial in the first honest court humanity has held in forty years.
about_author: Rosalind Zhou is a former maritime claims adjuster who turned to science fiction after a career spent documenting disasters no one wanted to name. She writes from a houseboat in Vancouver, where she keeps a ledger of every story she has ever abandoned.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Xanthe Reyes, POV. Between worlds that no longer speak, Xanthe works the insurance runs—documenting impossible accidents the Compact would rather bury. A cold open on her method: invisible, meticulous, paid to look away. When she files a report on a reactor 'failure' that was clearly sabotage, her handler burns it. Emotional beat: weary complicity, the cost of staying invisible.

chapters.title: Ship of Younger Ghosts
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The Vesper Kite docks at Meridian Station, forty years overdue, its crew aged backward—bodies twenty, memories of eighty. Xanthe is assigned the claim because she's 'good with anomalies.' The captain, Idris Okonkwo, recognizes her face from a file she has no memory of. Emotional beat: uncanny dread; the first crack in her self-containment.

chapters.title: Actuarial Mercy
chapters.summary: Idris's POV, flashbacks braided with the present. He recounts the Silence from inside it: the relay at Tau Ceti didn't fail—it was switched off, by Compact order, to conceal a terraforming collapse on Meridian's first colony, Halcyon Reach. The crew's rejuvenation came from an experimental protocol meant to make the evidence 'inadmissible.' Emotional beat: grief sharpened into testimony.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Cross-referencing old claims, she finds a pattern: every accident near the Silence corridor maps to Compact suppression. And one entry—dated the year of her own missing memory—bears her investigator signature. She never wrote it. Or she did, and it was taken from her. Emotional beat: vertigo; the investigator becomes the anomaly.

chapters.title: Handlers and Hounds
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Xanthe's handler, Deputy Director Sefa Vane, offers her a promotion that is obviously a leash. Meanwhile Compact security opens a file on the Vesper Kite's crew labeled 'asset recovery.' Idris disappears from the medical bay. Emotional beat: the trap closing; Xanthe realizes helping him means ending her old life.

chapters.title: What the Sleeper Fleet Dreams
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She infiltrates the Compact's cryosleep archive: two hundred thousand colonists in orbit, and a wake-order schedule that quietly excludes anyone flagged 'non-aligned.' Half of humanity, curated. She copies the schedule into her own neural cache, knowing it will be traceable. Emotional beat: cold fury hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Redacted Year
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, intercut with recovered fragments. Chasing her own file, she finds she once investigated Halcyon Reach itself—before the Silence—and was memory-wiped for it. The fragments surface in dreams: a colony dying of engineered drought, her testimony, a hand on her shoulder and a needle. Emotional beat: mourning for a self she can't fully recover.

chapters.title: Contraband Crew
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Xanthe finds Idris hiding in the Kite's gutted cargo hold with the surviving crew, who've become fugitives. They trust her exactly as far as her redacted file allows. She offers them the one thing she has: her access codes. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; trust built from shared damage.

chapters.title: Vane's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sefa Vane's POV. Inside the Compact's logic: waking all sleepers means resource collapse, so triage is mercy, not murder. Vane genuinely believes this—and offers Xanthe a place among the saved if she surrenders the ledger. Emotional beat: chilling reasonableness; power justifying itself in the language of care.

chapters.title: The Route Nobody Files
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The crew hijacks a maintenance skiff and runs the unlit corridor toward the Tau Ceti relay, dodging Compact patrols using Xanthe's knowledge of insurance flight plans. A near-miss with a patrol cutter costs them their fuel reserve and one crew member's nerve. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration; the invisible woman finally moving in the open.

chapters.title: Halcyon, Still Burning
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. They reach the dead colony. Halcyon Reach is preserved in vacuum—drought-cracked fields, a sealed administrative vault, and the mass graves the Compact's records call 'relocation.' Xanthe walks the settlement her younger self documented. Emotional beat: pilgrimage; grief given a place and a name.

chapters.title: The Vault Testimony
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the vault they find her original testimony—full, unredacted—recording that the Compact engineered the drought to test population-control protocols. Her own voice, forty years younger, names the directors. Including Vane's mentor. Emotional beat: the past handing her a weapon; identity restored at the worst possible price.

chapters.title: Signal Debt
chapters.summary: Crew engineer Priya Nair's POV. To broadcast the ledger, they need the relay at Tau Ceti switched back on—but the relay's AI demands a debt of signal: a complete, verified record before it will transmit. Verification requires the Compact's own cryptographic seal. Emotional beat: the dawning impossibility; the plan needs the enemy's key.

chapters.title: The Wake-Order Vote
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Back at Meridian, the Compact's directorate votes to accelerate the selective wake schedule—Vane must now decide whether Xanthe is a problem or a prototype. She chooses prototype: a public 'rescue' of the wayward investigator. Emotional beat: the antagonist's tragedy; conviction curdling into control.

chapters.title: Rescue as a Weapon
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Compact ships 'rescue' the Kite crew with staged tenderness, cameras running. Xanthe plays the grateful survivor while Vane privately shows her the wake-order console: her name is on the saved list, Idris's crew is not. Emotional beat: temptation offered in a velvet glove; the price of her own sleep.

chapters.title: The Key Is a Person
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The cryptographic seal isn't a code—it's the directorate's living quorum, four signatures given willingly or under duress. One director, old and dying, has been waiting forty years to confess. They reach her through the colony's last surviving relative: Priya. Emotional beat: fragile hope; the conspiracy has a hairline fracture.

chapters.title: Confession at Cryo Temperature
chapters.summary: Director Amara Sef's POV. In the cold archive, the dying director signs the seal and dictates her confession: the Silence, the drought, the curated waking. Vane's security team closes in. She buys the crew minutes with her last authority. Emotional beat: redemption arriving too late to be comfortable, but in time to matter.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Run
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The climax begins: Xanthe carries the sealed ledger through Meridian Station's underdecks toward the master antenna while Vane locks down the station. Chases, betrayals, a sacrifice by one of the Kite crew to hold a junction. Emotional beat: breathless momentum; every debt from the first sixteen chapters called in.

chapters.title: Everyone or No One
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, at the console. Confronted by Vane, Xanthe faces the choice the blurb promised: broadcast the ledger and force the wake of all—or accept the curated list and sleep. She transmits everything to every sleeper ship simultaneously: the crimes, the wake-order, the confession. The fleet's AIs, bound by their charters, begin waking everyone. Emotional beat: irrevocable commitment; terror transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: The Waking
chapters.summary: Multi-POV chorus. Two hundred thousand people wake to the truth in their ears. Stations hold or fracture by the hour; Vane, offered escape, instead orders her security forces to stand down—her arithmetic finally admitting a remainder it can't price. Idris's crew, rejuvenated and vindicated, becomes the first witness pool of the new order. Emotional beat: chaos with a spine of hope.

chapters.title: The First Honest Court
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Humanity convenes its first tribunal in forty years. Xanthe testifies—her old testimony and her new one, the redacted year and the recovered one—and then submits herself for judgment, because she once signed the reports that buried the truth. Vane stands beside her in the dock. Emotional beat: justice outside the law becoming justice through a law remade.

chapters.title: The Long Route, Reopened
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, coda. The relays come back online one by one; the colonies that no longer speak begin, tentatively, to speak. Xanthe takes a new contract—not to bury impossible accidents, but to investigate them in daylight. Final image: her ship departing Meridian, the sleeper fleet waking behind her like a sunrise. Emotional beat: earned peace; memory carried forward instead of erased.
